intent.raw_query: Iceland Northern Lights and hot springs, $3500 couple, January

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunting Tour
experiences.description: Join a guided evening tour away from Reykjavik's light pollution to witness the Aurora Borealis dancing across the sky. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and you'll learn about the science behind this natural phenomenon while capturing stunning photographs.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, silica mud masks, and steam caves while surrounded by dramatic lava fields. Book the Comfort package for access to the lagoon, a silica mud mask, and a drink at the in-water bar.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring dating back to 1891 surrounded by geothermal activity, bubbling geysers, and a small waterfall. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic experience offers a more intimate connection with Iceland's geothermal landscape.

experiences.name: Vatnajökull Glacier Hike
experiences.description: Strap on crampons and explore the largest glacier in Europe with a certified glacier guide. Trek across stunning ice formations, peer into brilliant blue crevasses, and learn about Iceland's rapidly changing glacial landscape. This guided hike offers an unforgettable encounter with Iceland's raw natural power.

experiences.name: Landmannalaugar Highland Hot Springs Trek
experiences.description: Hike through Iceland's surreal rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains in the Highlands and reward yourself with a soak in natural geothermal hot springs at the base camp. The vivid landscape of red, green, yellow, and purple volcanic rock is unlike anywhere else on Earth, making this a bucket-list nature experience.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Iceland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 06:10. Clear customs and collect luggage. Take the Flybus or a budget shuttle to Reykjavik BSI terminal, then arrange onward travel north toward Siglufjörður. The drive is approximately 4-5 hours via Route 1 and the Héðinsfjörður tunnel. Rest and recover from the flight during the journey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Siglufjörður in the early afternoon. Check in early if possible at Hotel Siglunes on Lækjargata 10, or store luggage and take a gentle walk along the harbour front to get oriented. Siglufjörður is a charming small fishing town nestled in a dramatic fjord — explore the colourful wooden houses and the quiet harbour area.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into the hotel and rest after the long travel day. As darkness falls (which comes early in January), step outside or find a dark spot near the harbour to watch for the Northern Lights — January is prime aurora season in Iceland. Dress in all your warmest layers.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or coffee at Keflavik Airport before departure — budget around 1,500–2,000 ISK for a pastry and coffee.
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches or snacks from a Reykjavik Bonus or Krónan supermarket during your transit stop to save money on the road.
meals.dinner: Kaffi Rauðka in Siglufjörður — a cosy local café and restaurant offering hearty Icelandic soups and fish dishes. Budget around 2,500–3,500 ISK for a main course.

day_by_day.notes: January days in Siglufjörður are very short — expect only about 4–5 hours of daylight. The Héðinsfjörður tunnel (opened 2010) connects Siglufjörður to Ólafsfjörður and makes access much easier. Check road conditions on road.is before driving as mountain roads can be icy or closed in January.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið) — one of Iceland's most celebrated regional museums, winner of the Council of Europe Museum Prize. It tells the fascinating story of the herring boom that made Siglufjörður prosperous. Entry is around 2,200 ISK. Note: confirm winter opening hours in advance as they may be limited.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the Siglufjörður town trail — a self-guided loop around the town taking in the old fish factory ruins, the church, and the scenic fjord views. The surrounding mountains are dramatic even in winter. If conditions allow, hike a short distance up the hillside above town for panoramic views of the fjord below.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights hunt from the hillside above Siglufjörður or along the fjord road away from town lights. The low light pollution in this remote area makes it excellent for aurora viewing. Check the Icelandic Met Office aurora forecast at en.vedur.is before heading out.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the hotel — pick up bread, skyr, eggs and fruit from the local Samkaup-Strax convenience store in Siglufjörður.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from supermarket supplies — skyr, rye bread with smoked salmon or cheese, and fruit. Eat at the museum café if open.
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal in the hotel if kitchen facilities are available, or return to Kaffi Rauðka for their fish soup — a warming and affordable option at around 1,800–2,200 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: The Herring Era Museum may have reduced winter hours — call ahead or check online. Stock up on groceries at the Samkaup-Strax store in town as options are limited and eating out every meal will strain a budget.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Ólafsfjörður via the Héðinsfjörður tunnel (about 20 minutes drive). Explore this equally charming small fishing village. Walk along the harbour and admire the mountain scenery surrounding the town — the peaks here are particularly dramatic in winter snow.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive back through the tunnel and continue to Dalvík, a slightly larger town about 45 minutes from Siglufjörður. Visit the Hvoll Museum which includes a quirky exhibit about the tallest man in Iceland. Walk along the Dalvík waterfront and enjoy views across Eyjafjörður toward Akureyri.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður before dark. Spend the evening watching for Northern Lights from the hotel or a dark spot along the fjord. If skies are clear, this is one of the best possible locations in Iceland for aurora viewing due to minimal light pollution.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — skyr with granola, coffee, and toast at the hotel.
meals.lunch: Grab a hot dog (pylsa) from a petrol station in Dalvík — Iceland's iconic budget snack at around 500–700 ISK each.
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner at the hotel — pasta with canned fish or a simple stew using ingredients from the local store. Budget around 1,000–1,500 ISK for ingredients.

day_by_day.notes: Fuel up the car in Dalvík or Ólafsfjörður as petrol stations in Siglufjörður may have limited hours. Always check road.is for tunnel and road conditions before driving in January.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Akureyri — Iceland's second largest city, about 1 hour from Siglufjörður via Dalvík and Route 82/1. Arrive and explore the compact city centre. Visit the iconic Akureyrarkirkja church perched on the hill above town — free entry and stunning architecture with beautiful stained glass windows.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Akureyri's main shopping street, Hafnarstræti, and browse the local shops. Visit the Akureyri Art Museum (Listasafnið á Akureyri) for a budget-friendly cultural experience — entry around 1,500 ISK. Walk along the waterfront and enjoy views of Eyjafjörður, Iceland's longest fjord.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Akureyri Swimming Pool (Sundlaug Akureyrar) — a fantastic budget activity at around 1,000–1,200 ISK entry. The outdoor hot pots are perfect for soaking while watching for Northern Lights on a clear evening. Return to Siglufjörður after your swim.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the hotel before departure.
meals.lunch: Akureyri has a Bonus supermarket — pick up supplies and eat a packed lunch, or try Bautinn restaurant for affordable traditional Icelandic food (soup of the day around 1,800 ISK).
meals.dinner: Strikið restaurant in Akureyri offers a good value lunch menu that sometimes extends to early evening, or try Greifinn for affordable pizza and pasta before the drive back. Budget 2,500–3,500 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: Akureyri is the main hub for the north — stock up on groceries at Bonus (Iceland's cheapest supermarket chain) to save significantly on food costs for the coming days. The drive back to Siglufjörður in the dark requires care on icy roads.

day_by_day.morning: Drive the Diamond Circle route — start with Goðafoss waterfall, about 45 minutes east of Akureyri on Route 1. This spectacular waterfall is one of Iceland's most beautiful and is free to visit. The name means 'Waterfall of the Gods' — in 1000 AD, a chieftain threw his Norse idols into it after Iceland adopted Christianity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Lake Mývatn, about 1 hour from Goðafoss. Visit the Námaskarð geothermal area (Hverir) — a surreal landscape of bubbling mud pots, steaming fumaroles and sulphur deposits. Completely free to visit and utterly otherworldly. Also explore the Mývatn lava fields (Dimmuborgir) — free walking trails through dramatic lava formations.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Mývatn Nature Baths (Jarðböðin við Mývatn) — a more affordable alternative to the Blue Lagoon at around 5,500 ISK entry. Soak in the geothermal lagoon surrounded by volcanic landscape. Then drive back to Siglufjörður (about 1.5 hours). Watch for Northern Lights on the return journey.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast before the long day trip.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from Bonus supplies eaten at Goðafoss or Mývatn — save money by avoiding the tourist cafés.
meals.dinner: Gamli Bærinn café near Mývatn for a warming bowl of lamb soup before the drive back, or self-cater on return. Budget 1,800–2,500 ISK if eating out.

day_by_day.notes: This is a long day — approximately 200km of driving round trip from Siglufjörður. Start early to make the most of the limited daylight hours. The Mývatn Nature Baths are significantly cheaper than the Blue Lagoon and equally beautiful. Dress in waterproof layers for the geothermal areas.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day in Siglufjörður. Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely morning. Take a slow walk around the town in the morning light — in January the golden hour lasts most of the day, creating beautiful photography conditions. Visit the small local church and explore the quieter back streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the area around Siglufjörður on foot. Walk along the fjord road south of town for views back toward the town with the mountains behind. Look for Arctic birds along the shoreline — Iceland in winter hosts various seabirds. The dramatic snow-covered peaks surrounding the fjord are spectacular on clear days.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights evening — this is a dedicated aurora hunt night. Drive a few kilometres out of town along the fjord road to escape any light pollution. Bring a thermos of hot chocolate, warm blankets, and a tripod if you have a camera. The forecast from en.vedur.is will indicate the best chances.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely self-catered breakfast — scrambled eggs, toast, skyr and coffee.
meals.lunch: Kaffi Rauðka for a treat — their fish soup or lamb soup is warming and reasonably priced at around 1,800–2,200 ISK.
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner — cook a hearty meal using Icelandic lamb mince (available at Samkaup-Strax) for a traditional kjötsúpa (lamb soup) experience at home.

day_by_day.notes: Rest days are important on a long trip, especially in harsh winter conditions. Use this day to do laundry, recharge devices, review photos, and plan the remaining days. Check the aurora forecast and weather for the week ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Drive the scenic Tröllaskagi peninsula — head south from Siglufjörður along Route 76 toward Hofsós. The drive through the mountains and along the coast is spectacular in winter. Stop at viewpoints along the way to photograph the fjords and snow-covered peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Hofsós, a tiny village on the east side of the Skagafjörður fjord. It is home to the Icelandic Emigration Centre (Vesturfarasetrið) which tells the story of Icelanders who emigrated to North America — entry around 1,500 ISK. The village also has a famous infinity-edge swimming pool overlooking the fjord (check winter opening hours).
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Siglufjörður via Sauðárkrókur — the largest town in Skagafjörður with a population of about 2,600. Stop for supplies at the local supermarket before returning north. Watch for Northern Lights on the evening drive back through the mountains.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast before the drive.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at a scenic viewpoint on the Tröllaskagi peninsula.
meals.dinner: Café in Sauðárkrókur — Kaffi Krókur or similar local café for a budget meal of soup and bread. Budget 1,800–2,500 ISK, or pick up groceries and cook at the hotel.

day_by_day.notes: The Hofsós swimming pool is one of Iceland's most scenic but may have limited winter hours — check ahead. The mountain roads on the Tröllaskagi peninsula can be challenging in winter — always check road.is. The total driving distance for this day trip is approximately 180km.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Varmahlíð in Skagafjörður valley, about 1 hour from Siglufjörður. Visit the Glaumbær turf farm museum — one of Iceland's best-preserved historic turf farmhouses, offering a fascinating glimpse into traditional Icelandic rural life. Entry around 2,000 ISK. The turf buildings date back to the 18th century.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Skagafjörður area — this region is famous for Icelandic horse breeding. Even in January you may spot herds of Icelandic horses in the fields. Drive along the valley and stop at the Víðimýrarkirkja turf church near Varmahlíð — one of Iceland's last remaining turf churches, free to view from outside.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður via the mountain road. Stop at the Reykir geothermal area near Varmahlíð if time allows — there is a small public hot pot (free or very low cost) that locals use. Arrive back in Siglufjörður for a quiet evening and Northern Lights watch.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the hotel.
meals.lunch: Café Aðalból at Glaumbær museum serves traditional Icelandic pancakes (pönnukökur) with cream and jam — a delicious and affordable treat at around 1,200–1,500 ISK.
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner at the hotel — use up remaining grocery supplies for a simple but satisfying meal.

day_by_day.notes: Glaumbær museum may have reduced winter hours — confirm before visiting. The Skagafjörður valley is one of Iceland's most historically rich areas and is well worth exploring. Icelandic horses are a unique breed and cannot be exported — seeing them in their natural winter environment is a special experience.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated Northern Lights morning — if there was a strong aurora display overnight, wake up early to catch any lingering activity. Otherwise, take a morning snowshoe walk or hike in the hills above Siglufjörður if conditions allow. The town is surrounded by excellent hiking terrain that transforms into a winter wonderland in January.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Siglufjörður Folk Music Centre (Þjóðlagasetur) if open — it celebrates Icelandic folk music traditions. Alternatively, spend the afternoon at the hotel reading, planning, or exploring the town's small art galleries and craft shops. Visit the local swimming pool (Sundlaug Siglufjarðar) for a warm soak — entry around 900–1,100 ISK.
day_by_day.evening: Aurora photography evening — if you have a smartphone with a night mode or a camera, set up on the harbour front or hillside for Northern Lights photography. The reflections of the aurora in the fjord waters can be spectacular. Bring hot drinks and dress in maximum layers.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — a warm porridge (hafragrautur) with skyr and berries is a traditional Icelandic winter breakfast.
meals.lunch: Kaffi Rauðka for a warming lunch — fish and chips or lamb soup. Budget 2,000–2,500 ISK.
meals.dinner: Self-catered — try making skyr cake (skyr kaka) for dessert using local skyr, a fun and budget-friendly Icelandic cooking experience.

day_by_day.notes: The local swimming pool is an essential Icelandic social institution — even small towns like Siglufjörður have excellent geothermally heated pools. This is where locals gather and it is a wonderful cultural experience as well as a great way to warm up. January aurora activity can be very high — check KP index forecasts.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Akureyri for a second visit — this time focus on the Botanical Garden (Lystigarðurinn), which is free to enter. While most plants are dormant in January, the garden's layout and the views over the fjord are still beautiful. Also visit the Nonni House (Nonnahús) — childhood home of author Jón Sveinsson, entry around 1,000 ISK.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Akureyri Christmas Garden (Jólahúsið) — Iceland's famous Christmas shop that is open year-round and free to browse. Walk along the waterfront and visit the Akureyri Museum (Minjasafnið á Akureyri) for local history — entry around 1,500 ISK. Stock up on Bonus supermarket supplies for the final days.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Akureyri Swimming Pool again for a relaxing soak in the outdoor hot pots before the drive back. Alternatively, if the Northern Lights forecast is strong, drive to a dark spot outside Akureyri — the area around Eyjafjörður offers excellent aurora viewing with the fjord as a foreground.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast before departure.
meals.lunch: Bonus supermarket picnic in Akureyri — fresh bread, cheese, smoked lamb (hangikjöt), and skyr. Very budget-friendly at around 1,000–1,500 ISK total.
meals.dinner: Brynja ice cream shop is an Akureyri institution — treat yourself to Iceland's famous ice cream even in winter (Icelanders eat ice cream year-round!). For a proper dinner, Strikið offers good value or cook at the hotel on return.

day_by_day.notes: Use this Akureyri visit to stock up on all remaining grocery needs from Bonus — it will be significantly cheaper than the Samkaup-Strax in Siglufjörður. Pick up any souvenirs from the Christmas Garden or local craft shops as prices are generally lower than in Reykjavik.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the area around Siglufjörður that you haven't yet visited. Drive north along the fjord road as far as it goes — the road ends at the old avalanche barriers above town, offering dramatic views. Learn about Siglufjörður's history with avalanches — the town has been hit several times and the protective barriers are an engineering feat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Siglufjörður swimming pool for a long, relaxing afternoon soak. The outdoor hot pots are perfect for a cold January afternoon. Alternatively, if there has been fresh snowfall, explore the snowy landscape around town on foot — the scenery is magical with fresh snow on the mountains.
day_by_day.evening: Final dedicated Northern Lights hunt of the trip. Drive to the darkest accessible spot near Siglufjörður — ideally along the fjord road away from town. Set up for a long aurora watch. January 2027 falls during a period of high solar activity (Solar Cycle 25 peak), making aurora sightings very likely on clear nights.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — use up remaining breakfast supplies.
meals.lunch: Kaffi Rauðka for a farewell lunch in Siglufjörður — try the catch of the day for an authentic local experience. Budget 2,500–3,000 ISK.
meals.dinner: Special self-catered dinner at the hotel — cook a traditional Icelandic lamb stew (kjötsúpa) using lamb, root vegetables, and herbs. A fitting final dinner in Iceland.

day_by_day.notes: This is likely your last full evening in Siglufjörður — make the most of the Northern Lights opportunity. The KP index forecast from en.vedur.is is your best tool for planning the evening. Even a KP2-3 can produce visible aurora at this latitude (66°N — above the Arctic Circle).

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Siglufjörður — take a last walk around the harbour and town. Visit any spots you missed during the trip. Take photographs of the town in the morning light. Check out of Hotel Siglunes and pack the car. Say goodbye to this remarkable little Arctic town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the drive south toward Reykjavik (approximately 4.5–5 hours). Stop at Blönduós on Route 1 for a break and fuel. Continue through the Holtavörðuheiði highland plateau — a dramatic and desolate winter landscape. Stop at Hraunfossar and Barnafoss waterfalls near Borgarnes if time allows — free to visit and spectacular.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Reykjavik in the early evening. Check into a budget hostel or guesthouse — options like Kex Hostel, Loft Hostel, or Reykjavik Downtown Hostel offer dorm beds from 4,000–6,000 ISK or private rooms from 12,000–18,000 ISK. Explore the Laugavegur street area and the old harbour.

meals.breakfast: Final self-catered breakfast at the hotel in Siglufjörður — use up all remaining food supplies.
meals.lunch: Petrol station stop in Blönduós — hot dog and coffee, the classic Icelandic road trip meal at around 800–1,000 ISK.
meals.dinner: Reykjavik has many budget options — Hlöllabátar (Icelandic submarine sandwiches) on Laugavegur is excellent value at around 1,500–2,000 ISK, or try Noodle Station for warming Asian noodle soup at around 1,800 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Siglufjörður to Reykjavik in January requires careful planning — check road.is thoroughly before departure. The highland sections of Route 1 can be icy. Allow extra time and do not rush. Book Reykjavik accommodation well in advance as January can still be busy with tourists.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Reykjavik — visit Hallgrímskirkja church (free to view outside, tower entry around 1,000 ISK for panoramic city views). Walk down Skólavörðustígur street to Laugavegur. Visit the Harpa Concert Hall on the harbour — free to enter the lobby and admire the stunning geometric glass architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Settlement Exhibition (Landnámssýningin) — an underground museum built around a Viking Age longhouse discovered beneath Reykjavik, entry around 2,200 ISK. Alternatively, the National Museum of Iceland (Þjóðminjasafn Íslands) offers excellent coverage of Icelandic history for around 2,500 ISK. Head to Keflavik Airport in the afternoon — allow 45–60 minutes for the drive plus 2–3 hours for check-in.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Keflavik International Airport. Reflect on 13 incredible days in Iceland — Northern Lights, geothermal hot springs, dramatic winter landscapes, and the unique culture of one of the world's most remote and remarkable countries.

meals.breakfast: Reykjavik Roasters or Te & Kaffi for a budget coffee and pastry — around 1,200–1,500 ISK. A treat for the final morning.
meals.lunch: Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur — Reykjavik's most famous hot dog stand near the harbour, a must-do Icelandic experience at around 600–700 ISK per hot dog.
meals.dinner: Airport meal or pack snacks for the flight — airport food is expensive so bring supplies from the city if possible.

day_by_day.notes: Return the rental car at Keflavik Airport — allow extra time for the return process. Do a final check of the accommodation and car for any left belongings. The Flybus from Reykjavik BSI to the airport runs regularly and costs around 3,500 ISK — book in advance online for the best price. Duty-free alcohol at Keflavik is significantly cheaper than in Reykjavik shops.

trip_options.title: Classic Iceland Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Keflavík International Airport at 06:10. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange car rental (recommended: 4WD for winter Iceland travel). Drive the scenic Ring Road north toward Siglufjörður — approximately 5–6 hours depending on road conditions. Stop at a petrol station for snacks and coffee to start the journey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the drive north through Akureyri, Iceland's second-largest city. Take a short stop to stretch your legs and grab lunch in Akureyri town center. Then continue the final stretch along the stunning Tröllaskagi Peninsula fjord roads to Siglufjörður, arriving at Hotel Siglunes in the late afternoon. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your room.
day_by_day.evening: Take a gentle evening stroll through the charming, quiet streets of Siglufjörður — one of Iceland's most picturesque fishing villages. Check the aurora forecast app (Vedur.is) and if conditions are favorable (clear skies, KP index ≥ 2), step outside the town toward the harbor or hillside for a first chance to spot the Northern Lights.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and pastry at the airport or a petrol station en route — Olis or N1 stations offer decent hot food options.
meals.lunch: Akureyri stop: Bautinn Restaurant on Hafnarstræti — a mid-range classic Icelandic diner with hearty soups and lamb dishes, perfect after a long drive.
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes restaurant or Kaffi Rauðka in Siglufjörður — a cozy local café-restaurant serving fresh fish and traditional Icelandic fare. Budget ~3,500–5,000 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: Road conditions in January can be challenging — check road.is before and during the drive. The Tröllaskagi tunnel (Héðinsfjörður Tunnel) makes the final approach to Siglufjörður much easier in winter. Arrival day is long; keep evening plans flexible and prioritize rest.

day_by_day.morning: After a well-deserved rest, enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast. Then explore Siglufjörður on foot — visit the award-winning Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið), which tells the fascinating story of the town's herring boom in the early 20th century. Open from 10:00; entry ~2,000 ISK.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or snowshoe up into the surrounding mountains for panoramic views of the fjord below. The hills around Siglufjörður offer accessible winter hiking with stunning scenery. Alternatively, visit the local swimming pool (Sundlaug Siglufjarðar) — a geothermal heated outdoor pool beloved by locals, perfect for warming up on a cold January afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights watch from the hillside above town or the harbor pier. Siglufjörður's remote location means minimal light pollution — excellent aurora viewing conditions when skies are clear. Bring a thermos of hot chocolate and a tripod for photography.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes breakfast buffet — included or available for ~1,500–2,000 ISK. Expect skyr, rye bread, smoked salmon, and eggs.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from a local grocery store (Krónan or Samkaup) — pick up bread, cheese, smoked lamb, and fruit for a self-catered fjord-side picnic or car lunch.
meals.dinner: Kaffi Rauðka — try the fish of the day or lamb soup. Warm, intimate atmosphere. Budget ~4,000–5,500 ISK per person with a drink.

day_by_day.notes: January daylight in Siglufjörður is very limited — roughly 5–6 hours of usable light (around 11:00–16:00). Plan outdoor activities accordingly. The local pool is a wonderful authentic Icelandic experience and costs only ~1,000 ISK.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south from Siglufjörður through the Tröllaskagi Peninsula toward Akureyri (~1.5 hours). Explore Akureyri's compact but charming town center — visit the iconic Akureyrarkirkja church perched on the hill, and browse the small shops along Hafnarstræti.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Mývatn Nature Baths (Jarðböðin við Mývatn) — a stunning geothermal lagoon set against a volcanic landscape, often called the 'Blue Lagoon of the North' but far less crowded. Soak in the mineral-rich, silica-blue waters at ~38–40°C. Entry ~5,500 ISK. The drive from Akureyri to Mývatn is about 1 hour east on Route 1.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Akureyri for dinner, then drive back to Siglufjörður (~1.5 hours). En route, keep eyes on the sky for Northern Lights — the open roads around Mývatn and the Tröllaskagi Peninsula are excellent aurora corridors.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes breakfast before departing.
meals.lunch: Akureyri: Bláa Kannan café on Hafnarstræti — a beloved local coffee house with soups, sandwiches, and homemade cakes. Budget ~2,000–3,000 ISK.
meals.dinner: Akureyri: Strikið Restaurant — mid-range with panoramic views over the fjord. Known for excellent lamb and Arctic char. Budget ~5,000–7,000 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book Mývatn Nature Baths in advance online — even in winter, popular time slots fill up. Bring a swimsuit and towel (rentals available on-site for ~700 ISK). The drive between Siglufjörður and Akureyri is scenic but can be icy — drive carefully.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Mývatn volcanic area. Depart early from Siglufjörður toward Mývatn (~2.5 hours). Explore the extraordinary Dimmuborgir lava formations — a surreal landscape of twisted lava pillars and caves, easily walkable in 1–2 hours. Also visit the Hverfjall volcanic crater rim for sweeping views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue around Lake Mývatn — visit the Skútustaðagígar pseudocraters (small craters formed by steam explosions) and the Námaskarð geothermal area (Hverir), a bubbling, steaming landscape of mud pots and fumaroles that feels otherworldly. Free to visit.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Siglufjörður. Stop at a roadside viewpoint for aurora watching if skies are clear. Arrive back at the hotel for a relaxed evening.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes breakfast.
meals.lunch: Mývatn: Vogafjós Farm Resort café — famous for their fresh geothermal bread baked underground and homemade skyr. A unique and affordable experience. Budget ~2,500–3,500 ISK.
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes restaurant or self-catered meal from groceries — pick up Icelandic lamb stew ingredients or ready-made soup from the local store.

day_by_day.notes: Hverir geothermal area has strong sulfur smells — normal and harmless. Stick to marked paths as the ground can be dangerously hot. Dimmuborgir is magical in winter with snow — bring good waterproof boots.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Siglufjörður area more deeply. Drive up the Héðinsfjörður valley (accessible via the tunnel) for dramatic winter mountain scenery and complete solitude. This abandoned fjord is hauntingly beautiful in winter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Siglufjörður and visit the Folk Music Center (Þjóðlagasetur) — a small but fascinating museum dedicated to Icelandic folk music traditions. Then relax at the local geothermal swimming pool for a warm afternoon soak.
day_by_day.evening: Dedicated Northern Lights evening. Drive 5–10 minutes outside of town to a dark spot near the fjord shore. Set up for aurora photography. The forecast-dependent activity is best enjoyed with patience and warm layers — temperatures can drop to -5°C or below.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes breakfast.
meals.lunch: Self-catered picnic in the car or at a scenic viewpoint — Icelandic rye bread with smoked lamb or gravlax from the local store.
meals.dinner: Kaffi Rauðka — try the lamb fillet or catch of the day. Cozy and warming after a cold evening outside. Budget ~4,000–5,500 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: Check aurora forecasts at en.vedur.is and the 'Aurora' app. A KP index of 2–3 is sufficient at Siglufjörður's latitude (66°N) for visible aurora. Even on cloudy nights, gaps in cloud cover can reveal stunning displays.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south toward the Snæfellsnes Peninsula — a long but spectacular drive (~4.5–5 hours from Siglufjörður). This is a travel day, so depart early. The route takes you through Borgarnes and along the north coast of the peninsula.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Snæfellsnes Peninsula. Visit Kirkjufell mountain and Kirkjufellsfoss waterfall — one of Iceland's most photographed landscapes, especially dramatic in winter with snow and ice. Continue to Snæfellsjökull National Park and the glacier-capped volcano at the tip of the peninsula.
day_by_day.evening: Check into a guesthouse or hotel in Grundarfjörður or Stykkishólmur for the night (pre-booked mid-range accommodation). Enjoy dinner in town and aurora watch from the harbor.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes breakfast before departing.
meals.lunch: Borgarnes: Settlement Center café — a good mid-journey stop with soups and sandwiches. Budget ~2,000–3,000 ISK.
meals.dinner: Grundarfjörður: Grundarfjörður Hostel restaurant or Bjargarsteinn Mathús — a well-regarded local restaurant with fresh seafood and lamb. Budget ~4,500–6,000 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: This is the longest driving day of the trip — approximately 5 hours. Check road conditions carefully. The Snæfellsnes Peninsula is stunning but roads can be icy and narrow in January. Consider staying two nights here to fully explore.

day_by_day.morning: Full day exploring Snæfellsnes Peninsula. Morning: Visit Djúpalónssandur black pebble beach and the dramatic sea cliffs at Lóndrangar basalt plugs. Walk the short trail to the beach and feel the raw power of the Atlantic Ocean in winter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Arnarstapi and Hellnar — two small fishing villages connected by a stunning coastal walking trail (about 2.5 km, 45 minutes). The basalt arch formations and sea caves along this trail are extraordinary. Then visit Vatnshellir lava tube cave (guided tours available, ~3,000 ISK).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Grundarfjörður or Stykkishólmur. Enjoy a relaxed dinner and aurora watch from the harbor — the Snæfellsnes Peninsula has excellent dark skies.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast or local bakery.
meals.lunch: Hellnar: Fjöruhúsið café — a charming cliffside café serving homemade soup, bread, and cake with incredible ocean views. A must-visit. Budget ~2,500–3,500 ISK.
meals.dinner: Stykkishólmur: Narfeyrarstofa — a beloved mid-range restaurant in a historic building, known for excellent lamb and fish dishes. Budget ~5,000–7,000 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: Vatnshellir cave tours run at set times — check in advance. The coastal walk between Arnarstapi and Hellnar can be slippery in winter; wear crampons or ice cleats. Fjöruhúsið café is a highlight of any Snæfellsnes visit.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Snæfellsnes toward Reykjavik (~2 hours). Check into your Reykjavik accommodation (pre-booked mid-range hotel or guesthouse in the city center). Drop bags and head out to explore the capital.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church (take the elevator to the top for panoramic city views, ~1,000 ISK). Walk down Skólavörðustígur to the colorful Laugavegur shopping street. Visit the Harpa Concert Hall on the waterfront — free to enter and architecturally stunning.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunting Tour — join a guided evening tour departing from Reykjavik. Professional guides take you away from city light pollution to optimal viewing locations, adjusting in real-time based on cloud cover and aurora activity. Tours typically run 21:00–00:00. Book in advance (~8,000–10,000 ISK per person).

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast or Grundarfjörður bakery before departing.
meals.lunch: Reykjavik: Bergsson Mathús — a popular mid-range café known for excellent soups, salads, and open-faced sandwiches. Budget ~2,500–3,500 ISK.
meals.dinner: Reykjavik: Sægreifinn (The Sea Baron) — a legendary harbor-side restaurant famous for lobster soup and grilled fish skewers. Affordable and authentic. Budget ~3,000–4,500 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: The Northern Lights Hunting Tour is one of the listed experiences — book through a reputable operator like Arctic Adventures or Reykjavik Excursions. Most tours offer a free rebooking if aurora conditions are poor.

day_by_day.morning: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa — depart Reykjavik early for the Blue Lagoon (~45 minutes drive toward Keflavík). Arrive for a morning slot (pre-booked essential — Comfort package recommended at ~12,000–15,000 ISK, includes silica mud mask and drink). Soak in the iconic milky-blue 38–40°C geothermal waters surrounded by lava fields.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Reykjavik by early afternoon. Visit the National Museum of Iceland (Þjóðminjasafn Íslands) on Suðurgata — excellent overview of Icelandic history from settlement to modern times. Entry ~2,500 ISK. Then explore the Old Harbor area.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Reykjavik's vibrant food and bar scene on Laugavegur and Austurstræti. Enjoy a relaxed dinner and perhaps a craft beer at a local bar.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the hotel before departing for Blue Lagoon — the spa has a café on-site.
meals.lunch: Blue Lagoon LAVA Restaurant (mid-range option) or the in-water bar for a lighter snack. Budget ~4,000–6,000 ISK for a meal.
meals.dinner: Reykjavik: Messinn — renowned for their cast-iron pan fish dishes. Mid-range and excellent quality. Budget ~5,000–7,000 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: Blue Lagoon MUST be pre-booked online — walk-ins are not accepted. Book the Comfort package minimum; the Premium package adds a towel and bathrobe. Arrive early to avoid crowds. Silica mud masks are included and great for skin.

day_by_day.morning: Golden Circle day trip from Reykjavik. Start at Þingvellir National Park — a UNESCO World Heritage Site where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet. Walk through the dramatic Almannagjá rift valley and visit the site of the ancient Icelandic parliament (Alþingi). Free entry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Geysir Geothermal Area — watch Strokkur geyser erupt every 5–10 minutes, shooting boiling water 20–30 meters into the air. Then visit Gullfoss waterfall — one of Iceland's most powerful and beautiful waterfalls, especially dramatic in winter with ice formations. Free entry.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavik. Optional: Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring in Flúðir is a slight detour on the Golden Circle route (~30 min off route) — Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring dating to 1891 surrounded by geysers and steam vents. Entry ~3,000 ISK. Return to Reykjavik for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Reykjavik.
meals.lunch: Geysir area: Geysir Center café — convenient stop with soup and sandwiches. Budget ~2,500–3,500 ISK. Or pack a lunch from a Reykjavik supermarket (Bónus or Krónan) to save money.
meals.dinner: Reykjavik: Snaps Bistro — a French-Icelandic bistro on Þórsgata, popular with locals. Excellent lamb and fish. Budget ~5,000–7,000 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: The Secret Lagoon is one of the listed experiences — highly recommended as a more authentic, less commercial alternative to the Blue Lagoon. If you visit both, do Secret Lagoon today and Blue Lagoon was yesterday. Gullfoss can be very icy — wear crampons.

day_by_day.morning: South Coast day trip from Reykjavik. Drive east along the South Coast to Seljalandsfoss waterfall — you can walk behind the curtain of water (may be icy/closed in January, check conditions). Continue to Skógafoss waterfall — massive and dramatic, with a staircase to the top for panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue east to Reynisfjara black sand beach near Vík — one of the world's most dramatic beaches with towering basalt columns (Reynisdrangar sea stacks) and powerful Atlantic waves. Exercise extreme caution — sneaker waves are dangerous year-round. Visit the nearby Dyrhólaey promontory for views of the coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavik (~2.5 hours). Enjoy a final Reykjavik evening with dinner and a walk along the illuminated harbor.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Vík: Suður-Vík restaurant — a cozy spot in the small village of Vík with good fish and lamb dishes. Budget ~3,000–4,500 ISK.
meals.dinner: Reykjavik: Grillmarkaðurinn (The Grill Market) — a mid-to-upper-range restaurant celebrating Icelandic ingredients with a modern twist. Budget ~6,000–9,000 ISK. Splurge-worthy for a special evening.

day_by_day.notes: NEVER turn your back on the ocean at Reynisfjara — sneaker waves have claimed lives. Stay well back from the waterline. Seljalandsfoss walkway behind the falls is often closed in winter due to ice — check locally. The South Coast is one of Iceland's most rewarding day trips.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Reykjavik back north toward Siglufjörður to collect any remaining belongings and enjoy a final night in the north. Alternatively, use this as a flexible day in Reykjavik for any missed activities, shopping on Laugavegur, or visiting the Reykjavik Art Museum.
day_by_day.afternoon: If returning north: stop at Borgarnes Settlement Center for a fascinating multimedia exhibition on the Norse settlement of Iceland and the Egils Saga. Entry ~2,500 ISK. Continue north through Varmahlíð and along the Skagafjörður valley — stunning winter scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back at Hotel Siglunes in Siglufjörður. Final Northern Lights watch from the harbor — the remote location and clear northern skies give one last excellent opportunity for aurora viewing.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Reykjavik.
meals.lunch: Borgarnes: Settlement Center café — soup and bread. Budget ~2,000–3,000 ISK.
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes restaurant — a farewell dinner with local fish or lamb. Budget ~4,500–6,000 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: This day offers flexibility — if you haven't yet seen the Northern Lights clearly, prioritize staying in the north where conditions are often better than Reykjavik. Alternatively, use the day for Reykjavik shopping and cultural activities before the flight home.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Siglufjörður. Take a slow farewell walk through the village, photograph the colorful harbor houses in the morning light, and enjoy a final soak at the local geothermal pool. Pack up and check out of Hotel Siglunes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive south from Siglufjörður toward Keflavík International Airport — approximately 5.5–6 hours. Depart by 10:00–11:00 to allow comfortable travel time. Stop in Akureyri for a final coffee and browse the duty-free-style local shops for Icelandic souvenirs (wool sweaters, lava salt, skyr products).
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavík Airport with time to spare. Browse the airport's duty-free shops for last-minute gifts (Icelandic wool, spirits, chocolate). Depart Iceland with memories of aurora-lit skies, steaming hot springs, and dramatic winter landscapes.

meals.breakfast: Final Hotel Siglunes breakfast — savor the skyr and smoked salmon one last time.
meals.lunch: Akureyri: Bláa Kannan café — a fitting farewell to the north with coffee and a pastry. Budget ~1,500–2,500 ISK.
meals.dinner: Keflavík Airport: Fljótt og Gott or Pylsuvagninn — airport dining options. Budget ~2,500–4,000 ISK. Or enjoy a meal at the airport's sit-down restaurant.

day_by_day.notes: Allow extra driving time in January — road conditions can slow travel significantly. Check road.is before departing. Return the rental car with a full tank (petrol stations near the airport: Orkan or N1 on the Reykjanes Peninsula). Arrive at the airport at least 2.5 hours before departure for international flights.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Iceland Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunting Tour
experiences.description: Join a guided evening tour away from Reykjavik's light pollution to witness the Aurora Borealis dancing across the sky. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and you'll learn about the science behind this natural phenomenon while capturing stunning photographs.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, silica mud masks, and steam caves while surrounded by dramatic lava fields. Book the Comfort package for access to the lagoon, a silica mud mask, and a drink at the in-water bar.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring dating back to 1891 surrounded by geothermal activity, bubbling geysers, and a small waterfall. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic experience offers a more intimate connection with Iceland's geothermal landscape.

experiences.name: Vatnajökull Glacier Hike
experiences.description: Strap on crampons and explore the largest glacier in Europe with a certified glacier guide. Trek across stunning ice formations, peer into brilliant blue crevasses, and learn about Iceland's rapidly changing glacial landscape. This guided hike offers an unforgettable encounter with Iceland's raw natural power.

experiences.name: Landmannalaugar Highland Hot Springs Trek
experiences.description: Hike through Iceland's surreal rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains in the Highlands and reward yourself with a soak in natural geothermal hot springs at the base camp. The vivid landscape of red, green, yellow, and purple volcanic rock is unlike anywhere else on Earth, making this a bucket-list nature experience.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Keflavík International Airport at 06:10. Clear customs and collect luggage. Transfer via private luxury vehicle (pre-arranged chauffeur service) toward Reykjavík for a brief orientation stop before beginning the scenic drive north toward Siglufjörður. The drive is approximately 5–6 hours; enjoy the dramatic winter landscape along Route 1 and the Tröllaskagi Peninsula.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the scenic drive north through Akureyri region and along the fjords. Stop at Goðafoss Waterfall ('Waterfall of the Gods') en route — a breathtaking frozen-edged cascade easily accessible from the Ring Road. Stretch your legs and photograph this iconic landmark before continuing to Siglufjörður.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Hotel Siglunes in Siglufjörður. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your premium accommodations overlooking the fjord. After dark, step outside or join a brief guided walk along the harbor to scan the skies for the Northern Lights — Siglufjörður's minimal light pollution makes it an excellent aurora-viewing location.

meals.breakfast: Light refreshments and coffee at Keflavík Airport's premium lounge (Saga Lounge if available) immediately after landing.
meals.lunch: Stop at Bautinn Restaurant in Akureyri — a well-regarded local institution serving hearty Icelandic lamb soup and fresh fish dishes, perfect for warming up mid-journey.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Hotel Siglunes' own restaurant, renowned for its locally sourced Arctic char, lamb, and seasonal Icelandic ingredients paired with a curated wine selection.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange your private airport transfer well in advance. Pack layers immediately accessible in carry-on — temperatures around Siglufjörður will be near 0–5°C with possible wind chill. Download the Icelandic Met Office aurora forecast app (vedur.is) to track aurora activity throughout the trip. January days are very short (roughly 5–6 hours of daylight), so plan driving during daylight hours carefully.

day_by_day.morning: After a leisurely breakfast at the hotel, explore Siglufjörður on foot. Visit the award-winning Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið) — one of Iceland's finest regional museums, housed in restored harbor warehouses. Learn about the town's dramatic herring boom history with beautifully curated exhibits.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive the scenic Héðinsfjörður tunnel route to neighboring Ólafsfjörður and explore the small coastal village. Return via the mountain road (weather permitting) for panoramic fjord views. Alternatively, arrange a private snowshoeing excursion on the slopes above Siglufjörður with a local guide — the surrounding mountains offer stunning winter terrain.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunting Tour — join a guided evening excursion departing from Siglufjörður into the surrounding countryside and elevated viewpoints above the fjord. Your guide will use real-time aurora forecasts and cloud-cover data to position the group optimally. Hot cocoa and warm blankets provided.

meals.breakfast: Full Icelandic breakfast at Hotel Siglunes — skyr, smoked salmon, rye bread, eggs, and fresh pastries.
meals.lunch: Café Rauðka in Siglufjörður — a charming local café serving homemade soups, open-faced sandwiches, and excellent coffee in a cozy atmosphere.
meals.dinner: Return to Hotel Siglunes for a premium dinner featuring pan-seared Arctic char with dill butter, roasted root vegetables, and Icelandic craft beer or wine pairing.

day_by_day.notes: Aurora activity depends on geomagnetic conditions (KP index) and cloud cover. January in northern Iceland offers some of the best aurora probability in the country. Dress in full thermal layers, waterproof outer shell, insulated boots, and gloves for the evening tour. The guided tour typically runs 3–4 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south along the Tröllaskagi Peninsula to Hofsós, a picturesque village on the eastern shore of Skagafjörður. Visit the Icelandic Emigration Center — a fascinating museum documenting the 19th-century emigration of Icelanders to North America. The drive itself offers spectacular fjord and mountain scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Sauðárkrókur, the largest town in Skagafjörður. Explore the local area and visit Glaumbær Folk Museum — a beautifully preserved turf farmhouse complex offering a window into traditional Icelandic rural life. The turf buildings are particularly atmospheric in winter snow.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður before dark. Enjoy a relaxing evening at the hotel. If aurora forecast is favorable (KP ≥ 3 and clear skies), head to the harbor or hillside viewpoints for independent aurora watching with a thermos of hot drink.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes breakfast buffet with fresh Icelandic dairy, smoked meats, and warm porridge.
meals.lunch: Mínervustofa Restaurant in Sauðárkrókur — a well-regarded local restaurant offering traditional Icelandic lamb and fish dishes in a warm, welcoming setting.
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes dinner — slow-braised Icelandic lamb shank with root vegetable purée and red wine reduction, followed by skyr panna cotta with crowberry compote.

day_by_day.notes: Road conditions on the Tröllaskagi Peninsula can be challenging in January. Check road.is (Vegagerðin) each morning for road closures or ice warnings. A 4WD vehicle is strongly recommended. Total driving today is approximately 120–150 km round trip.

day_by_day.morning: Drive approximately 45 minutes south to Akureyri, Iceland's 'Capital of the North.' Explore the charming town center — visit the iconic Akureyrarkirkja church perched on the hill, stroll the pedestrian Hafnarstræti street, and browse local boutiques and galleries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Akureyri Botanical Garden (Lystigarðurinn) — the world's northernmost botanical garden, serene and frost-covered in January. Then explore the Akureyri Art Museum (Listasafnið á Akureyri) for contemporary Icelandic art. Alternatively, arrange a private whale-watching tour from Akureyri harbor — humpback whales are sometimes spotted in Eyjafjörður in winter.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Akureyri before returning to Siglufjörður. If the aurora forecast is strong, pull over at a dark roadside viewpoint on the drive back for an impromptu aurora viewing session — the fjord roads offer spectacular unobstructed sky views.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes breakfast before departing.
meals.lunch: Rub23 Restaurant in Akureyri — one of Iceland's most celebrated restaurants outside Reykjavík, known for its creative sushi and Icelandic fusion cuisine with premium ingredients.
meals.dinner: Strikið Restaurant in Akureyri — a rooftop restaurant with panoramic fjord views, serving premium Icelandic steaks, fresh seafood, and an extensive wine list. Reserve in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Akureyri is approximately 75 km from Siglufjörður (about 1.5 hours via the Héðinsfjörður tunnels). Allow extra time for winter driving conditions. Akureyri has excellent shopping for Icelandic wool products (lopapeysa sweaters) and local design goods.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to the Lake Mývatn region (approximately 100 km east of Akureyri). Depart early to maximize the limited daylight. First stop: Goðafoss Waterfall for a proper visit with time for photography in the morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Mývatn area's volcanic wonders: Dimmuborgir lava formations (otherworldly dark lava pillars and arches), Hverfjall tephra crater (a perfectly formed volcanic ring), and the Námaskarð geothermal area (Hverir) — a surreal landscape of bubbling mud pools, steaming fumaroles, and sulfurous vents. The contrast of steam against the winter sky is extraordinary.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the Mývatn Nature Baths (Jarðböðin við Mývatn) — a premium geothermal lagoon with alkaline mineral-rich waters set against a dramatic volcanic landscape. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this is a deeply restorative experience. Enjoy the steam rising from the water into the cold night air, with potential aurora views overhead. Return to Siglufjörður.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Hotel Siglunes before departure.
meals.lunch: Vogafjós Farm Restaurant at Lake Mývatn — a unique farm-to-table experience where you can watch cows being milked through a glass window while dining on fresh geothermal rye bread, smoked trout, and farm-fresh dairy.
meals.dinner: Late dinner at Hotel Siglunes upon return — the kitchen can prepare a lighter supper of smoked lamb, cheese board, and Icelandic sourdough for a relaxed end to a full day.

day_by_day.notes: This is a long day (approximately 200 km round trip from Siglufjörður). Depart by 9:00 AM to make the most of daylight. The Mývatn Nature Baths are open until 22:00 — bring a swimsuit and towel (or rent on-site). The sulfur smell at Hverir is strong but harmless. Wear sturdy waterproof boots as the geothermal ground can be wet and uneven.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning at Hotel Siglunes after the previous day's long excursion. Enjoy a slow breakfast and take a leisurely walk along Siglufjörður's harbor waterfront. The town is beautifully quiet in winter — observe the fishing boats, colorful houses reflected in the fjord, and snow-capped peaks surrounding the village.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrange a private guided ski touring or snowshoeing experience on the mountains above Siglufjörður with a certified local mountain guide. The Siglufjörður area is renowned among backcountry skiers for its dramatic terrain. Non-skiers can enjoy a guided snowshoe hike to elevated viewpoints overlooking the fjord — spectacular in winter light.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunting Tour (second attempt, or independent viewing). Siglufjörður's position deep in a fjord surrounded by mountains creates natural darkness ideal for aurora viewing. Set up on the hillside above town or at the fjord's edge with a tripod for photography. The hotel can arrange a private aurora guide for a more personalized experience.

meals.breakfast: Extended leisurely breakfast at Hotel Siglunes — fresh waffles with Icelandic butter and jam, smoked salmon platter, and specialty coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café Rauðka in Siglufjörður — warm lamb soup, freshly baked bread, and a slice of homemade cake.
meals.dinner: Special premium dinner at Hotel Siglunes — request the chef's tasting menu (advance arrangement recommended): a multi-course celebration of Icelandic ingredients including langoustine bisque, reindeer tenderloin, and a skyr-based dessert with Icelandic berry coulis.

day_by_day.notes: Siglufjörður is one of Iceland's premier backcountry skiing destinations — if you ski, this is a world-class experience not to be missed. Equipment rental can be arranged through the hotel. January aurora probability in this latitude is high on clear nights — patience and warm clothing are essential.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Dalvík (approximately 60 km south of Siglufjörður) and take the Sæfari ferry to Hrísey Island — Iceland's second-largest island, known as the 'Pearl of Eyjafjörður.' Explore this tranquil island on foot or by guided jeep tour, spotting ptarmigan, Arctic foxes, and enjoying panoramic fjord views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return by ferry to Dalvík and drive to Árskógssandur to visit the Arctic Fox Center's northern outpost, or continue to explore the Tröllaskagi Peninsula's dramatic coastal scenery. Stop at Laufás, a historic turf farmhouse museum on the eastern shore of Eyjafjörður, beautifully preserved and atmospheric in winter.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður. Enjoy a relaxing evening with a private in-room spa treatment (arrange with the hotel in advance — some premium Icelandic hotels offer in-room massage services) followed by aurora watching from the hotel terrace or harbor.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes breakfast before departure.
meals.lunch: Packed premium lunch prepared by Hotel Siglunes kitchen — smoked lamb sandwiches, Icelandic cheese, fruit, and a thermos of hot soup for the island excursion.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Hotel Siglunes — pan-roasted cod with brown butter, capers, and potato gratin, paired with a crisp Icelandic craft beer or Chablis.

day_by_day.notes: Check the Sæfari ferry schedule in advance (runs multiple times daily in winter but can be affected by weather). Hrísey Island is extremely peaceful and offers a genuine off-the-beaten-path Icelandic experience. Dress warmly — the ferry crossing and island are exposed to wind.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Siglufjörður and begin the journey south toward the Golden Circle and South Iceland region. Drive via Akureyri and south along Route 1. Stop at Goðafoss one final time for a farewell photograph. Continue south through the dramatic highland interior (Route 1 via Möðrudalur if road conditions permit) or via the coastal route.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in the Geysir area of the Golden Circle. Visit Geysir geothermal field — witness the reliable Strokkur geyser erupting every 5–10 minutes, shooting boiling water 20–30 meters into the air. The surrounding geothermal landscape of hot springs, mud pools, and steaming vents is mesmerizing in winter.
day_by_day.evening: Check in at a premium Golden Circle area hotel (e.g., Hotel Geysir or Hótel Gullfoss — upgrade accommodation for this leg). After dark, join a Northern Lights Hunting Tour departing from the Golden Circle area — the open landscape offers wide, unobstructed sky views ideal for aurora hunting.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at Hotel Siglunes before checkout.
meals.lunch: Stop at a roadside restaurant in Akureyri or pack a hotel lunch for the long drive south.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Geysir Center Restaurant or Hotel Geysir's restaurant — fresh Icelandic lamb and fish dishes with views of the geothermal landscape.

day_by_day.notes: Today involves a long drive of approximately 350–400 km (5–6 hours). Depart by 8:00 AM to arrive before dark. Road conditions on Route 1 in January can include ice and snow — drive cautiously and check road.is. This marks the transition from the north to the classic South Iceland circuit.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Gullfoss Waterfall — one of Iceland's most iconic natural wonders. In winter, the falls are partially frozen with dramatic ice formations framing the thundering cascade. The golden canyon (Hvítá river gorge) is spectacular. Then visit Þingvellir National Park — a UNESCO World Heritage Site where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet and Iceland's ancient parliament (Alþingi) was founded in 930 AD.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to the South Coast. Stop at Seljalandsfoss Waterfall — in winter, the falls may be partially frozen and the path behind the waterfall (normally walkable in summer) creates extraordinary ice formations. Continue to Skógafoss Waterfall — another massive cascade with a rainbow in the mist on sunny days and ice columns in winter.
day_by_day.evening: Check in at a premium South Coast hotel (e.g., Hótel Rangá — Iceland's premier luxury rural hotel, renowned for its aurora viewing and fine dining). Enjoy the hotel's Northern Lights wake-up service — staff will call your room if the aurora appears overnight.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Golden Circle hotel before checkout.
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch at Þingvellir or stop at Friðheimar Greenhouse Restaurant (advance reservation essential) — a unique experience dining inside a working tomato greenhouse, with tomato-based dishes and fresh produce.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Hótel Rangá's Aurora Restaurant — one of Iceland's finest dining experiences, featuring a seasonal tasting menu with Icelandic langoustine, reindeer, and locally foraged ingredients. Exceptional wine cellar.

day_by_day.notes: Hótel Rangá is one of Iceland's most celebrated luxury properties and a world-class aurora-viewing destination. The hotel has its own telescopes for stargazing and aurora photography. Book well in advance. The South Coast drive today covers approximately 150 km.

day_by_day.morning: Vatnajökull Glacier Hike — depart with a certified glacier guide for an unforgettable hike on Europe's largest glacier. Strap on crampons and explore the ancient blue ice, crevasses, and ice caves of Vatnajökull. The glacier's ice caves are at their most spectacular in January — vivid blue ice formations carved by meltwater create cathedral-like chambers. This is a bucket-list experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon — a hauntingly beautiful lake filled with floating icebergs calved from Breiðamerkurjökull glacier. In winter, the lagoon may be partially frozen, with icebergs locked in ice. Walk to Diamond Beach (Breiðamerkursandur) where crystal-clear ice chunks wash up on the black volcanic sand — extraordinary photographic opportunities.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hótel Rangá. Enjoy the hotel's outdoor hot tubs under the open sky — perfect for aurora watching in warmth and comfort. The hotel's Northern Lights alert service ensures you won't miss any aurora activity.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at Hótel Rangá before the early departure.
meals.lunch: Packed premium lunch from Hótel Rangá for the glacier excursion — the guide will identify a sheltered spot on the glacier for a memorable lunch break.
meals.dinner: Return dinner at Hótel Rangá — celebrate the glacier adventure with a premium Icelandic seafood platter, followed by slow-cooked lamb with wild mushroom risotto.

day_by_day.notes: The glacier hike requires moderate fitness and appropriate clothing (provided or guided by the tour operator). Ice cave tours must be booked well in advance — they are extremely popular and limited in capacity. The drive from Hótel Rangá to Vatnajökull is approximately 2 hours each way. Depart by 7:30 AM.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to the Reykjanes Peninsula for the Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa experience. Book the premium Retreat Spa package — this includes access to the exclusive Retreat Lagoon (a private section of the Blue Lagoon), in-water massage, silica mud mask treatment, algae mask, and access to the luxurious Retreat Hotel facilities. The milky-blue geothermal waters at 37–39°C are deeply therapeutic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue enjoying the Blue Lagoon's premium facilities — the Lava Restaurant within the Blue Lagoon complex offers an exceptional dining experience. Explore the surrounding lava field landscape, unique to the Reykjanes Peninsula. Visit the Reykjanes UNESCO Global Geopark visitor center to understand the extraordinary volcanic geology of the peninsula.
day_by_day.evening: Drive to Reykjavík (approximately 50 minutes from the Blue Lagoon). Check in at a premium Reykjavík hotel (e.g., The Retreat at Blue Lagoon, or Hotel Borg in central Reykjavík — a historic luxury property). Explore Reykjavík's vibrant evening scene on Laugavegur street.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Hótel Rangá before checkout and departure.
meals.lunch: Lava Restaurant at the Blue Lagoon — an award-winning restaurant built into the lava rock, serving Icelandic seafood, lamb, and vegetarian dishes with views over the steaming lagoon. A truly unique dining setting.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Dill Restaurant in Reykjavík — Iceland's first Michelin-starred restaurant, offering a New Nordic tasting menu celebrating Icelandic ingredients and culinary heritage. Advance reservation essential.

day_by_day.notes: Blue Lagoon Retreat Spa packages must be booked months in advance — this is one of Iceland's most sought-after luxury experiences. Arrive at your booked time slot. The Retreat package includes a bathrobe, slippers, and towel. Silica mud masks are complimentary. Avoid submerging hair in the lagoon as silica can be drying.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Reykjavík's cultural highlights: visit Hallgrímskirkja church (take the elevator to the tower for panoramic city views), the Harpa Concert Hall (stunning geometric glass architecture on the harbor), and the National Museum of Iceland (Þjóðminjasafn Íslands) for a comprehensive overview of Icelandic history and culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring excursion — drive approximately 1.5 hours east to Flúðir to visit Iceland's oldest swimming pool (1891). This natural hot spring is far more intimate and authentic than the Blue Lagoon, surrounded by geothermal activity including a small geyser that erupts regularly. Soak in the 38–40°C waters surrounded by steam and snow-covered landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavík. Explore the city's renowned restaurant and bar scene. Visit the Kolaportið flea market area or the Grandi harbor district. Join a final Northern Lights Hunting Tour departing from Reykjavík — guides take groups to dark-sky locations outside the city for optimal aurora viewing on this penultimate night.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Reykjavík hotel — Hotel Borg's breakfast is particularly celebrated for its quality and variety.
meals.lunch: Messinn Restaurant in Reykjavík — famous for its cast-iron pan-served fresh fish of the day, a beloved local institution for seafood lovers.
meals.dinner: Grillið Restaurant at Radisson Blu Saga Hotel — Reykjavík's iconic rooftop fine dining restaurant with panoramic city views, serving premium Icelandic steaks, lamb, and seafood with an extensive wine list.

day_by_day.notes: The Secret Lagoon is significantly less commercialized than the Blue Lagoon and offers a more authentic Icelandic hot spring experience. Admission is modest but the experience is premium. Combine with a visit to the nearby Flúðir village. The evening Northern Lights tour from Reykjavík typically runs 3–4 hours and includes transportation.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. Enjoy a leisurely farewell breakfast at your Reykjavík hotel. Take a final walk along the Reykjavík harbor waterfront — visit the iconic Sólfar (Sun Voyager) sculpture, a gleaming steel Viking ship silhouette against the backdrop of Mount Esja and the sea. Browse Laugavegur street for last-minute Icelandic souvenirs: lopapeysa wool sweaters, Icelandic sea salt, skyr, and local design goods.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, visit the Settlement Exhibition (Landnámssýningin) — a fascinating underground museum built around a 10th-century Viking longhouse discovered beneath central Reykjavík. Alternatively, visit the Reykjavík Art Museum (Listasafn Reykjavíkur) for a final dose of Icelandic contemporary art. Transfer to Keflavík International Airport (approximately 45 minutes from Reykjavík) via private luxury chauffeur.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Keflavík International Airport. Relax in the Saga Lounge (available with business class or Priority Pass) before your flight. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of aurora hunting, geothermal soaking, glacier hiking, and immersion in Iceland's raw, otherworldly nature.

meals.breakfast: Extended farewell breakfast at your Reykjavík hotel — savor every last bite of Icelandic skyr, smoked salmon, and fresh pastries.
meals.lunch: Snaps Bistro in Reykjavík — a beloved French-Icelandic bistro serving excellent fish of the day, steak tartare, and classic bistro fare in a warm, convivial atmosphere. A perfect final Reykjavík lunch.
meals.dinner: Airport dining at Keflavík — the Saga Lounge offers light refreshments and drinks. Alternatively, dine at the airport's Fiskmarkaðurinn (Fish Market) outlet for a final taste of Icelandic seafood before departure.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for the drive to Keflavík and airport check-in/security. Pre-arrange your private airport transfer. Iceland's duty-free shop at Keflavík is excellent for Icelandic spirits (Brennivín), chocolates, and last-minute gifts. Ensure all aurora photographs are backed up before departure. This concludes a world-class 13-day premium Iceland winter experience.
